articles.headline: Raphinha admits struggling to play after De Miguel's death: 'Could have happened to me'
articles.description: Barcelona captain Raphinha paid an emotional tribute to late Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel after scoring a brace in the Champions League victory over Aston Villa.
articles.headlineJa: ラフィーニャ、デ・ミゲルの死後にプレーすることの苦しさを吐露：「自分にも起こり得たこと」
articles.descriptionJa: バルセロナの主将ラフィーニャは、チャンピオンズリーグのアストン・ヴィラ戦で2ゴールを挙げた後、亡くなったテネリフェの選手ヘスス・デ・ミゲルに感情のこもった追悼の意を表した。
articles.body:
Barcelona forward Raphinha said it was difficult to play Tuesday's UEFA Champions League game against Aston Villa after learning of the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel.

De Miguel died after he suffered a cardiac arrest following an on-field collision with Real Oviedo goalkeeper Jesús Owono on Monday. He was 30.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation [RFEF] announced no domestic games would be played on Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday as Spanish football mourns De Miguel.

However, Tuesday's Champions League fixtures went ahead, with Raphinha scoring twice as Barça beat Premier League side Villa 3-0 at Spotify Camp Nou.

"Wherever [De Miguel] is, I hope he finds his way," Raphinha told Movistar after the game. "I want to send his family strength ... and today, not talk about football.

"After I saw the news, I didn't feel good. In the end, he was a fellow football player. This could have happened to any of us. It could have happened to me.

"It's very difficult to go out and play a game in these circumstances. He was a player who was the same age as me. Maybe that's why it affected me so much."

As a mark or respect, the Champions League hymn was not played before kick-off at Camp Nou, with a minute's silence held for De Miguel instead.

Barça coach Hansi Flick said the news hit Raphinha hard.

"What happened in Tenerife, I think it affected him a lot, like everyone of us," Flick said in the post-game news conference.

"Our deepest condolences to the family, the club, the friends, everyone ... it's a big tragedy. I think it's affected him a lot."

Despite everything, Raphinha managed to continue his incredible form at the start of the season, scoring twice after Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring as Barça ended Villa's perfect start in the Champions League this season.

Raphinha, playing as a No.9, has now scored 19 goals in all competitions this term -- more than anyone else in Europe's top five leagues -- and Flick has backed him to keep finding the net at the same rate.

"I have no doubts about [him maintaining that rhythm]," he said. "He is in a good mood and a good moment right now. I am really happy with him. He's an amazing player."

Barça's victory was slightly tainted by an injury to Rodri. The midfielder was replaced by Marc Bernal, with a top-of-the-table clash against Atlético Madrid in the league looming on Sunday.

"He had some discomfort," Flick announced. "We have to wait until [Thursday] for the tests."

LaLiga leaders Barça travel to Atlético on Sunday having rebuilt some confidence after back-to-back losses to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid at the end of October.

They returned to winning ways with a 6-1 hammering of Alavés at the weekend and, in keeping Villa's attack out, kept their first clean sheet in the Champions League in 18 games.

"It was important we defend together, very compact and the last line played an amazing level," Flick said.

articles.headline: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard completes knee treatment, begins 'return to play process'
articles.description: Kawhi Leonard has completed a treatment to address left knee swelling and is beginning the "return to play process" in Toronto, the Raptors announced.
articles.headlineJa: ラプターズのカワイ・レナード、膝の治療を完了し「復帰プロセス」を開始
articles.descriptionJa: ラプターズの発表によると、カワイ・レナードは左膝の腫れの治療を完了し、トロントで「復帰プロセス」を開始している。
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard has completed a treatment to address left knee swelling and is beginning the "return to play process" in Toronto, the Raptors announced Tuesday.

The team said it will issue another update in one week. 

Leonard, 35, was sidelined because of left knee swelling after appearing in just two regular-season games for Toronto. An MRI on the knee last month showed no structural damage.

Leonard has previously had issues with his right knee, having multiple surgeries for his meniscus and ACL. 

In two games this season, Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals. He's in his first year back with the Raptors after being traded to Toronto from the LA Clippers this offseason after a scandal-marred conclusion to his six seasons there. He agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors after the trade.

Leonard previously played one season in Toronto, leading the Raptors to their only NBA championship in 2019 before leaving for the Clippers in free agency.

articles.headline: Lamine Yamal makes history as ruthless Barça end Aston Villa's perfect UCL start
articles.description: Aston Villa had their chances, but Barça's relentless press and red-hot duo of Lamine Yamal and Raphinha proved too much in a comprehensive Champions League victory.
articles.headlineJa: ラミン・ヤマルが歴史を刻む、容赦ないバルサがアストン・ヴィラのUCL完璧なスタートを阻止
articles.descriptionJa: アストン・ヴィラにもチャンスはあったが、バルサの執拗なプレスと、絶好調なラミン・ヤマルとラフィーニャのコンビが、チャンピオンズリーグでの圧倒的な勝利を決定づけた。
articles.body:
BARCELONA, Spain -- Raphinha and Lamine Yamal proved too hot for Aston Villa on Tuesday as free-scoring Barcelona recorded a 3-0 win at Camp Nou to end the Premier League side's perfect start in the UEFA Champions League this season.

Yamal opened the scoring in the seventh minute, capitalizing on a João Gomes mistake to overtake Kylian Mbappé as the highest-scoring teenager in the competition's history with 14 goals. Raphinha, excelling as a No. 9 once again, then sealed the victory with a second-half brace, taking him to 19 goals for the season in just 13 appearances.

The win moves Barça level in the standings on nine points with Villa, who had won all three of their European matches heading into the meeting with the LaLiga leaders.

In the lashing rain, Barça started quickly with Yamal's goal, but Villa came back, creating good chances for Matty Cash and Gomes in front of the vocal away support. Johan Manzambi also came close for Villa, but Barça remained a threat at the other end and pulled away from the Premier League side in the second half.

There was an element of fortune to Raphinha's 52nd-minute goal, with his strike deflected past the helpless Zion Suzuki. There was no luck to the second goal, though, a poacher's finish after brilliant work from João Cancelo.

Fermín López and Yamal, on two occasions, came close to adding a fourth as Barça continue to rebuild their momentum after back-to-back losses to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid last month.

Saturday's 6-1 hammering of Alaves helped restore confidence ahead of Villa's visit, and this win sets Hansi Flick's side up nicely for Sunday's top-of-the-table clash against Atlético Madrid in LaLiga.

- As it happened: Barça thump Villa, Man Utd rally to beat Roma

- Did Man United's Champions League comeback save Carrick's job?

- City relegated from Premier League but win the UCL? How it could play out

Raphinha, Yamal outduel Villa

If it's any consolation to Villa, they are not the first team to be undone by Europe's most effective attacking duo. Yamal and Raphinha have netted 32 of Barça's 60 goals this season in just 15 matches.

Yamal went first here. Barça's press forced Gomes into an error and the Brazilian will have been horrified as he saw the ball drop to the youngster through the rain. Cutting inside on his left foot, Yamal shaped a trademark finish around Suzuki to set the home side on its way.

Raphinha stepped up in the second half. His goal scoring since Flick took over in 2024 has been impressive, but he has reached a new dimension this season playing as a striker. His seventh Champions League double extended his lead as the top scorer in Europe's top five leagues this season across all competitions. He now has 19; Mbappé is second with 15.

The Brazilian striker will be particularly pleased with his second goal, a true striker's finish as he got across his marker to turn home Cancelo's cross. He now has 23 Champions League goals for Barça, tied with Robert Lewandowsk

articles.headline: Michael Carrick: Man United comeback win over Roma 'an important night'
articles.description: Michael Carrick hailed an "important night" after Manchester United came from behind to beat Roma, but insisted he wouldn't get carried away with "one win."
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・キャリック：マン・ユナイテッドのローマ戦逆転勝利は「重要な夜」
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドが逆転でローマを下したことを受け、マイケル・キャリックは「重要な夜」だったと称えたが、「一度の勝利」で浮かれすぎることはないと強調した。
articles.body:
Michael Carrick hailed an "important night" after Manchester United came from behind to beat Roma, but insisted he wouldn't get carried away with "one win."

United fought back from 2-0 down to win 3-2 at Old Trafford on Tuesday and register their first victory in 10 games.

Carrick said afterwards he was "proud" of his players, although he stopped short of branding the result a turning point in the season.

"I'm not getting too carried away with things," said Carrick.

"I think it's an important night. But we've got to take stock, we've got to stay calm and prepare and be ready for another big game on the weekend."

Carrick remains under pressure with United sitting 17th in the Premier League table and only above the relegation zone on goal difference.

The win over Roma ended a run of three straight defeats, but the 45-year-old insisted there was no feeling of relief at the final whistle.

- Bruno Fernandes: Michael Carrick was right to drop me from Man United XI

- Did Man United's Champions League comeback save Carrick's job?

- Man United fans throw tennis balls on field before stunning comeback

"Genuinely, no," he said. "Whether that's right or wrong, or normal or not, I don't know, but I didn't feel relief. I was genuinely pleased for the players.

"I could feel their willingness to do well, and so for them to have to dig really deep, and just for everybody, you know.

"I feel the responsibility of that, so to see everybody having that feeling that we all crave. That's why we're all here. I really 100% wasn't thinking about myself at that moment -- it was just more seeing everybody and the feeling that we can generate when we do things right."

articles.headline: Saints release veteran kicker Daniel Carlson after he posted 2nd-worst FG% in NFL
articles.description: Veteran kicker Daniel Carlson, whose 66.7% accuracy on field goals was tied for second worst in the NFL this season, was released by the Saints on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: セインツ、NFLでワースト2位のFG成功率を記録したベテランキッカーのダニエル・カールソンを放出
articles.descriptionJa: 今シーズンのフィールドゴール成功率が66.7%でNFLワースト2位タイとなったベテランキッカーのダニエル・カールソンが、火曜日にセインツから放出された。
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- The Saints have released veteran kicker Daniel Carlson, the team announced Tuesday.

Carlson, 31, struggled with consistency during his short time as the Saints' kicker and made only 66.7% of his kicks (8-of-12) this season. That was tied for the second-worst percentage in the league, ahead of only Harrison Mevis, who was cut by the Los Angeles Rams earlier in the season. Carlson also missed two PAT attempts in seven games.

Releasing Carlson is the second move the Saints have made coming out of the bye week after they started the season 2-5. They also announced the firing of run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti on Monday after the team rushed for only 18 yards on 17 attempts in a 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris before the bye.

The kicking issue was one of several areas of scrutiny the Saints faced after the loss to the Steelers, in which Carlson missed a 52-yard field goal. Saints coach Kellen Moore said the position would be evaluated during the bye but did not commit to a major change on Monday.

"Obviously we just got to continue to evaluate the field goal opportunities," Moore said on Monday. "And so that'd be something that we'll just have to work through and discuss and find the best solution for Sunday."

Moore also said on Monday they did not plan to bring in any kickers for tryouts.

The release of Carlson paves the way for Irish practice squad kicker Charlie Smyth to kick against the Cleveland Browns this Sunday. Smyth, who came to the Saints via the International Player Pathway in 2024, spent most of his first two seasons on the practice squad. He was elevated as the Saints' full-time kicker for the final six games of last season after they released Blake Grupe, and he made 75% of his kicks (12-of-16 ).

Smyth and former UFL kicker Tanner Brown competed for the starting spot in training camp, but Carlson was signed in late August after neither kicker showed enough consistency to win the job.

Carlson had spent several months as a free agent before signing with the Saints. He had previously been with the Las Vegas Raiders for eight seasons and was an All-Pro in 2021 and 2022 but was not re-signed after he made only 81.5% of his kicks.

The Saints also claimed running back Audric Estime off waivers from the Browns. Estime was with the Saints for seven games in 2025 and their 2026 training camp but was released with an injury settlement in September.

articles.body:
The New York Giants and cornerback Greg Newsome II have reached agreement on a three-year, $46 million extension, his agent, Erik Burkhardt of Roc Nation Sports, told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The deal comes halfway through Newsome's first season with the Giants and includes $32 million in guaranteed money.

A first-round pick of the Cleveland Browns in 2021, he was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars last October before signing a one-year deal this past offseason with the Giants.

Newsome, 26, has 17 tackles, six passes defended and one interception this season for a New York team that, at 4-2-1, sits atop the NFC East standings.

articles.headline: Bills release C.J. Gardner-Johnson after one-game spitting suspension
articles.description: The Bills have released safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, the team announced Tuesday.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills released safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson on Tuesday, just six games into his tenure with the team and one day removed from his suspension for spitting at an opponent being completed.

Gardner-Johnson, 28, signed with the Bills over the offseason and started the team's first six games before he was ejected just before halftime against the Las Vegas Raiders for spitting in the direction of tight end Brock Bowers. Over his six games with Buffalo, Gardner-Johnson registered 26 tackles with two pass breakups and one interception.

After moving on from Gardner-Johnson, the Bills' options at safety include veterans Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone and rookie Jalon Kilgore. Hamlin and Stone were Buffalo's active safeties for its Week 8 win over Baltimore while Gardner-Johnson was serving his suspension, and the sense within the building is that the options on the roster played well enough to justify longer looks at the job with or without Gardner-Johnson in the fold.

Hamlin, Stone and Kilgore are also more valuable special teams options than Gardner-Johnson, who didn't play any special teams snaps through the first six weeks.

Before signing with Buffalo, Gardner-Johnson played for six teams in the past five years. He won a Super Bowl as a member of the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles.

articles.headline: Man City relegated from Premier League but win Champions League? How it could play out
articles.description: What would happen to Man City's superstar players if they get relegated from the Premier League but qualify for Champions League?
articles.body:
It has been over a month since the Premier League announced that Manchester City had been found guilty on 114 different charges of cheating the league's financial rules and obstructing the investigation into their potential cheating of the league's financial rules.

And ... we're still just sitting in limbo. Man City continue to play and win most of their matches, while none of us know what any of it really means.

They could be competing for another title. They could be wasting our time with meaningless matches that are about to get voided from the season. They could actually be in the middle of a relegation battle from a points deduction.

It's worth emphasizing: We're talking about the team that's currently in second place in the most popular league for the world's most popular sport -- and we don't know the stakes of any of the games they're playing! A speedy resolution -- or at least, a speedy resolution before the inevitable appeals process -- is necessary.

But until then, we're left to ponder the nature of reality in the wholly made-up structures of a made-up sport, and we're left to theorize about what might come next. So, theorize we will.

Given how harsh the language and the verdict were against City and -- how forceful City have been in their denials of their documented wrongdoing -- it seems likely at this point that the club will be relegated from the Premier League. Somehow, some way.

So, let's say that happens. You know what could also happen? Manchester City could win the Champions League.

Frankly, if they do get relegated from the Premier League via a massive points deduction or whatever other means soon, City might be even more likely to win the Champions League than they currently are. Sportsbooks, right now, have them as the sixth favorites -- after Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, Arsenal, Bayern Munich, and Real Madrid -- with implied odds of about 10% to lift the European Cup.

So, then, let's say that both of those things happen: Manchester City get relegated from the Premier League, and Manchester City win the UEFA Champions League. If they did complete the dubious double, what would happen next?

How Manchester City could win the Champions League

I'm not so sure what Man City's relegation would look like in practice. But in a sense, it doesn't really matter.

I mean, it does matter. If City are given, say, a 100-point deduction or something, then the rest of the season means nothing to them. They'd still have to play games, but the stakes of those games would be no different than a situation in which the Premier League announced that City were no longer in the league and would play no more games for the rest of the season.

Both situations have all kinds of knock-on effects. If City are forced to play the rest of the season, then what about the teams that had to play City before they had nothing to play for? Is it fair for half of the league to get two games against a team that isn't trying and the other half to get

articles.headline: Josh Allen-produced short doc on Buffalo storm gets release date, trailer
articles.description: The short documentary on the once-in-a-generation Buffalo blizzard will be released on Nov. 24.
articles.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. -- The unlikely pairing of Academy Award-winning director Ben Proudfoot and Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is bringing a quintessential Buffalo story to HBO Max.

The documentary short "The Buffalo Miracle," directed by Proudfoot and executive-produced by Allen and his production company Out of Pocket Studios, is set to premiere on the streaming service on Nov. 24. It depicts the true story of Buffalo fast-food workers who opened their doors to strangers and neighbors as places of refuge during the historic Christmas-week blizzard of 2022.

A once-in-a-generation storm that brought hurricane-force winds of up to 80 mph, 15-foot-high snowdrifts and wind chill temperatures around 30 below zero, the storm was a monster that meant whiteout conditions and loss of power and access to infrastructure across the region.

The trailer plays on Buffalo's nickname as the "City of Good Neighbors," and highlights how common love for the Bills brings the whole town together, especially in December when the team is preparing for a playoff run. Allen led the Bills to a 13-3 record in 2022, but the Bills were on the road for a Week 16 matchup against the Chicago Bears during the blizzard's peak.

Allen has become increasingly involved in film and production work in recent years. In addition to his frequent commercial work, he launched Out of Pocket Studios over the summer. The company already produces multiple programs for Paramount in addition to the upcoming documentary.

Proudfoot is a two-time Oscar winner for the documentary shorts "The Queen of Basketball" and "The Last Repair Shop."

The film will premiere the week of Thanksgiving, when Allen and the Bills will host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium for a primetime AFC showdown.

articles.headline: Dumonts take over as controlling owners of Mavericks
articles.description: Sivan and Patrick Dumont purchased Miriam Adelson's shares of the Mavericks last month, making the Dumont family the controlling owners of the franchise.
articles.headlineJa: デュモン家がマベリックスの筆頭オーナーに就任
articles.descriptionJa: シヴァンとパトリック・デュモンが先月、ミリアム・アデルソンのマベリックス株式を取得し、デュモン家が同球団の支配権を持つオーナーとなった。
articles.body:
Sivan and Patrick Dumont purchased Miriam Adelson's shares of the Dallas Mavericks last month, making the Dumont family the controlling owners of the franchise with a 69% share.
Adelson has had minimal involvement with the Mavericks since she bought the majority share of the franchise from Mark Cuban in December 2023 along with her daughter and son-in-law. Patrick Dumont has served as the Mavericks' governor since the families took control of the franchise.

"It's really about long-term investment in the city of Dallas," Dumont told ESPN on Tuesday. "The Dumont family is really committed to building what we hope is the best arena in the NBA, a really significant investment in the city that will help create the new 40-year home for the Dallas Mavericks, a great experience for our fans and inspire our team to win championships. That's really what we're focused on. We had the opportunity, and we're really excited about it."

Cuban, who has expressed regret about selling the Mavericks to Adelson and the Dumonts due to being frozen out of the franchise's basketball and business operations, maintains a 27% share of the franchise. According to the terms of the 2023 sale, Dumont can purchase another 20% share from Cuban at the original $3.5 billion valuation.

"Our plan is to look at that and to do that over time," Dumont said. "I just have to tell you: I love Mark. He's been a great family friend for a really long time. He's just a super passionate Mavs fan and he's frustrated. I respect it. We're going to hopefully do him proud. That's my goal -- to make all of our Mavs fans super proud about the success of the team and win a championship."

Dumont, the Las Vegas Sands Co. CEO, has overseen a major overhaul of the franchise during his turbulent tenure as the Mavericks governor.

Dumont drew intense wrath from the fanbase for approving former general manager Nico Harrison's decision to trade perennial MVP candidate Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers months after the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals. Dumont has since taken drastic measures to attempt to position the franchise for success as it pivots to build around Cooper Flagg, the reigning Rookie of the Year who Dallas drafted with the No. 1 overall pick after a historic stroke of lottery luck.

"The most important thing every day is just trying to work harder to get better," Dumont said. "It's something that really applies in life, but it's something that really applies to here. It's been an experience as a new owner in the league. Dallas is a great sports city. I think we have the best fans in the NBA, very passionate, and it's my job to make sure that we win and that we support our fans. I'm really focused on that. I've learned that there are a lot of things you can do -- sometimes they work, sometimes they don't -- but you've got to keep pushing, got to keep going."
